The PKGBUILD file defines a standard build process for the `livewdf-git` package, which is a real-time audio circuit simulator. It fetches source code from two trusted Git repositories: the primary upstream at `https://github.com/Yahiake/LiveWDF` and the JUCE framework from its official repository `https://github.com/juce-framework/JUCE.git`. Both sources are declared explicitly and use the `git+https` protocol, which is secure and appropriate for AUR packages.

The build process initializes a Git submodule for JUCE but uses a cached local copy from the `source` array instead of fetching externally during build time. This is done securely via `git config submodule.modules/JUCE.url "$srcdir/JUCE"` and `git submodule update --init`, ensuring that only the version specified in the source is used. There are no network operations during `build()`, `check()`, or `package()`, and no use of dangerous patterns like `eval`, obfuscated code, or runtime downloads. All checksums are set to 'SKIP', which is expected and acceptable for Git-based packages in the AUR, especially `-git` packages where content is inherently mutable.

The package installs binaries, VST3 plugin, desktop entries, and appropriate license files into standard system directories using safe `install` and `cp` commands. No system modifications, privilege escalations, or data exfiltration mechanisms are present. The operations are confined to the package build and install tree, and all actions align with standard AUR packaging practices for a C++/CMake-based audio application depending on the JUCE framework.
</details>
